For each condition of ambient temperature (T ) and thermal load (𝑊 ), the condenser amb ℎ𝑒𝑎𝑡𝑒𝑟 coolant inlet temperatures (𝑇 ) were set as high as possible to maintain the lowest possible fan power 𝐶𝑁𝐷 𝑤,𝑖 and, as a result, to reduce the total system power, given that the radiator fan is the main contributor to the tank’s energy consumption. The condenser coolant inlet temperatures (𝑇 ), however, are typically limited by vapor high (T ) 𝐶𝑁𝐷 𝑤,𝑖 vap,high and vapor mid temperatures (T ), which must remain a few degrees lower than the fluid’s saturation vap,mid temperature to avoid rapid pressure rise and consequent venting of the system. In other words, the coolant temperatures near the fluid’s saturation indicate insufficient condenser cooling for a given thermal load. Although higher condenser coolant inlet temperatures (𝑇 ) are desired to reduce PUE, they also 𝐶𝑁𝐷 𝑤,𝑖 lower the amount of air in the vapor space of the tank, which can increase vapor losses in a poorly sealed lid. Typically, the vapor high temperature (T ) should not be higher than about 3°C below the fluid’s vap,high boiling temperature [20], [21]. An alarm can be set in the tank to shut down the IT equipment in case that temperature limit is reached. Alternatively, the vapor mid temperature (T ), the probe for which is vap,mid typically placed below the vapor high probe, ideally should not reach the fluid’s boiling temperature.
